memory: I believe that success is an equation with many variables, but if I had to narrow it down, I'd say it comes down to three things: discipline, adaptability, and relationships. Discipline gets you in the game—showing up every day, putting in the work, and staying consistent even when things don't go your way. Adaptability is what keeps you in the game—markets shift, industries change, and if you can't pivot, you'll get left behind. And relationships? They determine how far you'll go. No one builds anything meaningful alone. The people you surround yourself with—mentors, colleagues, clients, even competitors—shape your trajectory more than you realize. Every major opportunity in my career can be traced back to a relationship I nurtured years earlier.I believe that resilience is a crucial component of success in finance. While intelligence and talent are important, they are not enough on their own. The ability to handle rejection and keep moving forward is essential for achieving long-term success. I have experienced setbacks in my career, including losing a major deal with Intelligent Motors. However, with the guidance of a mentor, I learned to view these setbacks as opportunities for growth and learning. By adopting a mindset that sees failures as tuition fees for future success, I was able to overcome my fears and continue pushing forward. This perspective has been instrumental in my career advancement and has helped me achieve greater success in the long run.I believe that creating your own luck is crucial for achieving success. Many people believe that successful individuals were simply in the right place at the right time, but this is not the case. Luck favors those who actively put themselves in positions where opportunities can find them. It's essential to be proactive and take the initiative to create opportunities rather than waiting for them to arise. By reaching out to industry leaders and asking specific questions, I was able to establish valuable connections that opened doors to new opportunities. This approach has been instrumental in my career advancement and has allowed me to achieve greater success.I believe that betting on oneself is crucial for career advancement. Many young professionals wait for validation or permission to take risks, but the truth is, opportunities are created by taking ownership and stepping up. By taking on responsibility and figuring things out as you go, you can grow into a role before even having the title. It's essential to act like a leader, think like an investor, and operate like a CEO before you have the corresponding titles. This mindset will make you undeniable and attract opportunities that align with your capabilities. I have seen this approach work in my own career, and I encourage others to take the same path.I believe that long-term success is not just about achieving milestones, but also about sustaining them. While it's possible to have a successful year or make a big deal, true success comes from consistently making good decisions, managing risk, and staying humble enough to keep learning. I've seen individuals who made significant amounts of money overnight only to lose it quickly because they didn't develop the habits necessary to sustain their success. The key to lasting success is to remain hungry and curious, avoiding complacency that can arise from short-term wins. It's essential to continue growing and learning, as growth is the ultimate indicator of enduring success.
